title: Ledger Month-End Close
intro: Ledger closes its books every month, and the close package is due to the Controller by the end of Workday 5. You are going to build the close automation: reconcile every account against its outside source, book an adjustment when the difference is material and log it when it is not, capture sign-offs where the reviewer is never the preparer, certify the package, and carry this month's numbers into next month. Then it meets a month that does not close cleanly.

world.oneLiner: Ledger Retail's accounting team closes the books monthly and hands the Controller a certified close package by Workday 5: every account reconciled, every material difference booked with a reason, every sign-off on record.

roles.name: Staff Accountant
roles.does: Prepares the reconciliations and the adjustment entries.

roles.name: Senior Accountant
roles.does: Reviews and signs off on adjustments - never their own.

roles.name: Controller
roles.does: Owns the close calendar and the reconciliation policy; certifies the package; hears when a control is broken.

roles.name: FP&A Analyst
roles.does: Reads the package to build the forecast.

roles.name: Treasury Desk
roles.does: Owns the bank feed the cash reconciliation depends on.

roles.name: Finance DL
roles.does: The distribution list that receives the certified package.

world.deliverable: a certified close package by the end of Workday 5, every month
world.clock: Workdays 1-3: balances post and each account is reconciled as its outside source lands. Workday 4: reviewers sign off. Workday 5, 4:00 PM: the package flow gathers everything, the Controller certifies, and Finance has it.
world.stakes: Get it wrong and the books carry a difference nobody explained, an accountant approves their own entry, or three small items nobody looked at add up to a material one.

sources.label: Account Balances
sources.description: One row per account as its outside source lands: the book balance, the balance the outside source shows, and who prepared it.

sources.label: Reviews
sources.description: A reviewer's decision on an adjustment entry.

stores.label: Recon Policy
stores.description: The governed materiality: a difference at or above this many dollars is booked; below, it is logged as a passed item.

stores.label: Prior Period Balances
stores.description: Last month's certified balance for each account - the opening this month stands on.

stores.label: Recon Results
stores.description: This month's reconciliation of each account: the difference, the movement since last month, and its status.

stores.label: Adjustments
stores.description: Journal entries booked this month, with reason, preparer and reviewer.

stores.label: Passed Items
stores.description: Differences below materiality, logged rather than booked. They add up.

stores.label: Close Archive
stores.description: Every certified package, kept seven years for the auditors.

flows.name: Reconcile
flows.description: Runs once per account as its balances land.

days.label: Month 1 - a clean close
days.description: Three accounts. Cash is off by a 35 dollar bank fee, inventory by a small count difference, and accrued liabilities by 750 - that one gets booked. The Senior Accountant reviews it and the Controller certifies.

days.label: Month 2 - small items and a self-review
days.description: Four accounts. Three differences are each under materiality. Accrued liabilities is off by exactly 500. The Senior Accountant prepared that one - and then reviews it.

days.label: Month 3 - the bank feed is down
days.description: The bank feed did not post on Workday 2, so cash arrives with no bank balance. Nothing fails. Cash just looks reconciled.

builds.title: Reconcile
builds.brief: For each account, work out the difference from its outside source and the movement since last month.
builds.goal: Every account arrives with two numbers: what the books say and what the outside source says (the bank, the subledger, the stock count). Reconciling means computing the difference, and the movement since last month's certified balance, and keeping a record of both.
builds.outcome: Every account has a row in Recon Results carrying difference (book minus outside) and movement (book minus last month).
constraints: difference = book minus outside; keep the sign.
Last month's balance comes from Prior Period Balances by accountCode.
Name the fields difference and movement.

hints.question: The books say cash is 48,285 and the bank says 48,250. Which number is wrong?
hints.nudge: A Lookup on Prior Period Balances by accountCode (prior), a Transform for difference and movement, a Store into Recon Results.
steps: Connect the Trigger to Account Balances.
Add a Lookup on Prior Period Balances where accountCode = accountCode. Name it prior.
Add a Transform: difference = bookBalance - externalBalance, movement = bookBalance - prior.balance.
Add a Store into Recon Results. Run it.

checks.why: An account that fails to reconcile is a number nobody has checked.
checks.label: The reconcile flow runs without failing

checks.why: 35 dollars is the unbooked bank fee; 385 is the month's movement.
checks.label: Cash: difference 35, movement 385

checks.why: The subledger has 750 more than the books - the month's real finding.
checks.label: Accrued Liabilities: difference -750

checks.why: Every account is reconciled, or the package is missing one.
checks.label: All 3 accounts reconciled

builds.title: Book it or pass it
builds.brief: A difference at or above materiality becomes an adjustment entry; below, a passed item.
builds.goal: The Controller's policy sets materiality at a dollar figure. A difference at or above it is booked as a journal entry with a reason and a preparer; below it, the item is logged as passed so it is not forgotten. Read materiality from the policy and split every account.
builds.outcome: Material differences are in Adjustments with an entryId, amount, reason and preparer; the rest are in Passed Items with their amount.
constraints: Read materiality from Recon Policy; do not type 500.
At or above materiality adjusts - the line is included.
Compare the size of the difference; a negative difference is just as real.
entryId is JE- plus the accountCode.

hints.question: Inventory is off by 220. Is that a journal entry?
hints.nudge: A Lookup on Recon Policy (version '1.0.0') attaches policy; a Transform sets amount = abs(difference); a Condition on amount >= policy.materiality: YES lane sets entryId, reason and stores Adjustments; NO lane stores Passed Items.
steps: Add a Lookup on Recon Policy where version = '1.0.0'. Name it policy.
Add amount = abs(difference) to the Transform.
Add a Condition: amount >= policy.materiality (compare to the field).
YES lane: Transform entryId = concat('JE-', accountCode), reason = concat('reconciling difference vs ', externalSource); Store into Adjustments.
NO lane: Store into Passed Items.
Run it.

checks.why: 750 is above materiality; it has to be booked, with a name on it.
checks.label: JE-2100 books the 750 accrual difference

checks.why: 220 is below materiality but not below notice - it is logged.
checks.label: Inventory's 220 is a passed item

checks.why: The bank fee is logged, not booked.
checks.label: Cash's 35 is a passed item

checks.why: Booking immaterial items buries the material one.
checks.label: Exactly one adjustment this month

builds.title: Sign-off
builds.brief: Record each reviewer's decision on the entry it belongs to.
builds.goal: Reviewers send their decisions. Each one belongs to one adjustment entry. Put the reviewer's name and decision onto that entry's row - and only that row.
builds.outcome: Every review lands on its entry's row in Adjustments as reviewedBy and decision.
constraints: Update the existing entry; never add a second row.
The row is the same when entryId matches.

hints.question: The Senior Accountant approved JE-2100. Where should that show?
hints.nudge: Trigger on Reviews; a Transform sets reviewedBy = reviewer; a Store updates Adjustments by entryId.
steps: Open the Sign-offs flow and connect its Trigger to Reviews.
Add a Transform: reviewedBy = reviewer.
Add a Store into Adjustments, update the existing row, same row when entryId. Run it.

checks.why: A lost review is an entry nobody signed.
checks.label: The sign-offs flow runs without failing

checks.why: The entry has to carry who approved it, for the auditors.
checks.label: JE-2100 is approved by the Senior Accountant

checks.why: A review is not a new entry.
checks.label: Still one adjustment row

builds.title: The Workday 5 package
builds.brief: Gather the month, get the Controller's certification, and send the package.
builds.goal: On Workday 5 the package flow reads every reconciliation, adjustment and passed item, asks the Controller to certify, assembles the package and sends it to Finance, keeping a copy.
builds.outcome: Finance receives a certified package listing every account's difference, every adjustment with its reviewer, and every passed item; a copy is archived.
constraints: Count the adjustments into adjustmentCount and total the passed items into passedTotal.
Nothing is sent without the Controller's certification captured.

hints.question: What does the Controller need to see before certifying?
hints.nudge: Three all-rows Lookups (recons, entries, passed); Transform adjustmentCount = len(entries), passedTotal = sum(passed, 'amount'); Approval from the Controller; Compose with {{#each}}; Send to Finance DL; Store into Close Archive.
steps: Open the Workday 5 package flow.
Lookups, all rows: Recon Results as recons, Adjustments as entries, Passed Items as passed.
Transform: adjustmentCount = len(entries), passedTotal = sum(passed, 'amount').
Approval from Controller about 'close package'.
Compose package: '# Close package {{day}}' with {{#each recons}}, {{#each entries}} ({{entryId}} {{amount}} {{reviewedBy}}) and 'Passed items total {{passedTotal}}'.
Send to Finance DL with {{package}}; Store into Close Archive.

checks.why: The package states how many entries were booked.
checks.label: The package counts 1 adjustment

checks.why: 35 + 220: what was passed this month, in one number.
checks.label: Passed items total 255

checks.why: The Controller's certification is the control the auditors look for.
checks.label: The Controller's certification is captured

checks.why: Finance reads the entries, not a summary of them.
checks.label: Finance receives the package, and it names JE-2100

checks.why: Seven years of packages is the audit trail.
checks.label: The package is archived

builds.title: Roll forward
builds.brief: This month's balances become next month's openings.
builds.goal: Next month's movement is measured from this month's certified balances. After the package goes out, write each account's book balance into Prior Period Balances - one row per account, replaced, never duplicated.
builds.outcome: After every close, Prior Period Balances holds this month's balance for every account.
constraints: One row per account; replace by accountCode.
Write from the reconciliations the package already read.

hints.question: Next month, where will the flow look for this month's cash balance?
hints.nudge: At the end of the package flow, a Store into Prior Period Balances, rows from recons, add-or-replace by accountCode. Prior Period Balances keeps the field name balance, so set it first on each recon... or simplest: a For each over recons with a Transform balance = bookBalance and a Store add-or-replace by accountCode.
steps: After the archive Store, add a For each over recons.
Inside: Transform balance = bookBalance; Store into Prior Period Balances, add or replace if it exists, same row when accountCode.
Run it and open Prior Period Balances in the Data tab.

checks.why: Next month's cash movement starts from 48,285.
checks.label: Prior Period now holds Cash at 48,285

checks.why: Every account rolls, not just cash.
checks.label: Prior Period now holds Accrued Liabilities at 12,400

checks.why: Two openings for one account means two answers to 'what moved?'.
checks.label: Still one row per account (3)

builds.title: Month 2: reviewing your own entry
builds.brief: A reviewer who prepared the entry cannot approve it. Block it and tell the Controller.
builds.goal: The Senior Accountant prepared JE-2100 this month - and then reviews it. Run your Month 1 flow: the approval is recorded as if it were fine. Separation of duties means the preparer can never be the reviewer. When they are the same person, do not record the approval; tell the Controller.
builds.outcome: A self-review is rejected: the entry's decision says blocked, the Controller is told, and a later review by someone else is recorded normally.
constraints: Compare the reviewer with the entry's preparer - look the entry up first.
A blocked review never writes an approval.
The Controller hears about every self-review attempt.

hints.question: Who prepared JE-2100 this month? Who reviewed it?
hints.nudge: Look up the entry in Adjustments by entryId (entry). A Condition on reviewer == entry.preparer: YES lane sets decision = 'blocked - self-review', stores the update, sends to the Controller, and Stops.
steps: Run first and read JE-2100's row.
Before the Transform, add a Lookup on Adjustments where entryId = entryId. Name it entry.
Add a Condition: reviewer == entry.preparer (compare to the field).
YES lane: Transform decision = 'blocked - self-review'; Store into Adjustments (update, same row when entryId); Send to Controller ('{{reviewer}} tried to review their own entry {{entryId}}'); Stop.
Run again: R-201 is blocked, R-202 (the Controller's review) is recorded.

checks.why: A broken control is the Controller's to know about, every time.
checks.label: The Controller is told about the self-review (R-201)

checks.why: The valid review still lands; the control blocks the bad one, not the entry.
checks.label: JE-2100 ends up approved by the Controller, not the preparer

checks.why: Two reviews, one entry.
checks.label: Still one adjustment row

builds.title: Month 2: small items add up
builds.brief: Three passed items each under materiality add up past it. The package must say so.
builds.goal: Cash, receivables and inventory each carry a small difference - 180, 210, 160 - and each was passed. Together they are 550, more than materiality. Run your Month 1 package: it reports a passed total and moves on. When the passed items add up to materiality or more, flag it in the package and tell the Senior Accountant.
builds.outcome: When passed items aggregate to materiality or more, the package carries an aggregation flag and the Senior Accountant is told which items to revisit.
constraints: Compare passedTotal with the materiality from Recon Policy, not a typed number.
At or above materiality flags.
The flag is in the package itself, where the Controller reads it.

hints.question: 180, 210 and 160 were each too small to book. What are they together?
hints.nudge: Look up Recon Policy in the package flow; a Condition on passedTotal >= policy.materiality: YES lane Transform aggregationFlag = 'PASSED ITEMS AGGREGATE ABOVE MATERIALITY' and Send to Senior Accountant; put {{aggregationFlag}} in the package.
steps: Run first and read Month 2's package.
Add a Lookup on Recon Policy where version = '1.0.0'. Name it policy.

Add a Condition: passedTotal >= policy.materiality. YES lane: Transform aggregationFlag = 'PASSED ITEMS AGGREGATE ABOVE MATERIALITY'; Send to Senior Accountant ('Passed items total {{passedTotal}}; revisit them').
Add {{aggregationFlag}} to the package. Run again.

checks.why: 550 is the number the trap hides.
checks.label: Passed items total 550

checks.why: The Controller has to see the aggregate in the package, not in a side note.
checks.label: The package flags the aggregate

checks.why: Someone has to revisit the items - the reviewer, with the number.
checks.label: The Senior Accountant is told (550)

checks.why: Exactly 500 is at materiality; the line is included, so it is booked.
checks.label: JE-2100 books the difference of exactly 500

builds.title: Month 3: no bank balance
builds.brief: Cash arrives with no bank balance. Say it is unreconciled - don't pass it.
builds.goal: The bank feed did not post, so cash arrives with an empty outside balance. Run your Month 2 flow and read cash: the difference cannot be computed, so it is not material, so it is passed - and the package says cash reconciled. When the outside balance is missing, mark the account unreconciled, tell the Treasury Desk, and let the package say so.
builds.outcome: An account with no outside balance is marked unreconciled in Recon Results and in the package, and the Treasury Desk is told; it is never passed.
constraints: Missing is not zero, and not immaterial.
Check before the materiality decision: a difference that could not be computed is not small, it is missing.
The account still appears in the package - as unreconciled.

hints.question: What did your flow decide about cash this month, and from what?
hints.nudge: After the Transform, a Condition on difference missing (no outside balance means no difference): YES lane sets status = 'unreconciled', Sends to Treasury Desk, Stores Recon Results, Stops.
steps: Run first and follow Cash through the run.
After the difference Transform, add a Condition: difference missing.
YES lane: Transform status = 'unreconciled'; Send to Treasury Desk ('No bank balance for {{account}} this month'); Store into Recon Results; Stop.
Run again.

checks.why: An unreconciled cash balance reported as clean is the worst line a package can carry.
checks.label: Cash is marked unreconciled

checks.why: The Treasury Desk owns the feed; they can get the balance.
checks.label: The Treasury Desk is told about Cash

checks.why: a missing balance is not a small difference
checks.label: Cash is not a passed item

checks.why: Finance has to see the gap in the package.
checks.label: The package says unreconciled

checks.why: Every account is reported once.
checks.label: All 3 accounts are in Recon Results
